hypsilophodon:enwiki:3.title: Hypsilophodon (First specimens and the debate of distinctiveness)

facts.statement: Hypsilophodon lived during the Early Cretaceous period.
facts.quote: fossil_range: Early Cretaceous,

facts.statement: The genus Hypsilophodon was named by Thomas Henry Huxley in 1869.
facts.quote: parent_authority: Huxley, 1869

facts.statement: The first remains of Hypsilophodon were discovered in 1849.
facts.quote: The first remains of Hypsilophodon were found in 1849

facts.statement: The type species, Hypsilophodon foxii, was formally named in 1869.
facts.quote: the type species, Hypsilophodon foxii, was named in 1869

facts.statement: Hypsilophodon is a neornithischian dinosaur from the Early Cretaceous of England.
facts.quote: Hypsilophodon (; meaning "Hypsilophus-tooth") is a neornithischian dinosaur genus from the Early Cretaceous period of England

facts.statement: Hypsilophodon had a pointed head with a sharp beak used for biting off plant material, similar to modern parrots.
facts.quote: It had a pointed head equipped with a sharp beak used to bite off plant material, much like modern-day parrots

facts.statement: Abundant fossils found on the Isle of Wight provide a clear picture of the species' build.
facts.quote: Abundant fossil discoveries were made on the Isle of Wight, giving a good impression of the build of the species

facts.statement: The first specimen was recovered in 1849 from the Wessex Formation near Cowleaze Chine on the south-west coast of the Isle of Wight.
facts.quote: The first specimen of Hypsilophodon was recovered in 1849, when workers dug up the soon-called Mantell-Bowerbank block from an outcrop of the Wessex Formation, part of the Wealden Group, about one hundred yards west of Cowleaze Chine, on the south-west coast of Isle of Wight

facts.statement: Richard Owen studied the first halves of the specimen in 1855 and initially classified it as a young Iguanodon.
facts.quote: Richard Owen studied both halves and, in 1855, published a short article on the specimen, considering it to be a young Iguanodon rather than a new taxon

facts.statement: In 1867, Thomas Henry Huxley concluded that the specimen was a distinct animal from Iguanodon after comparing its vertebrae and metatarsals.
facts.quote: This was unquestioned until 1867, when Thomas Henry Huxley compared the vertebrae and metatarsals of the specimen more closely to those of known Iguanodon, and concluded that it must be a different animal entirely

facts.statement: The species was named Hypsilophodon foxii, with the holotype being a skull discovered by William Fox.
facts.quote: The species was named Hypsilophodon foxii, and the holotype was the Fox skull (which today has the inventory number NHM NHMUK PV R 197)

facts.statement: Huxley classified Hypsilophodon in the family Iguanodontidae, noting its relationship to Iguanodon and Hadrosaurus.
facts.quote: Huxley classified Hypsilophodon taxonomically, considering it to belong to the family Iguanodontidae, related to Iguanodon and Hadrosaurus

facts.statement: The generic name Hypsilophodon means "Hypsilophus-tooth".
facts.quote: Hypsilophodon thus means "Hypsilophus-tooth"

facts.statement: The Greek root in the name refers to the high crest of a lizard, not to the teeth of the dinosaur, which are not high-ridged.
facts.quote: The Greek ὑψίλοφος, hypsilophos, means "high-crested" and refers to the back frill of the lizard, not to the teeth of Hypsilophodon itself, which are not high-ridged in any case

facts.statement: John Whitaker Hulke returned to the fossil beds on the Isle of Wight to collect additional material.
facts.quote: John Whitaker Hulke returned to the Hypsilophodon fossil bed on the Isle of Wight to obtain more material

facts.statement: Hulke changed his opinion after obtaining two new, more informative specimens.
facts.quote: Hulke had by then shifted his opinion, having obtained two new more informative specimens

facts.statement: Hulke published his findings confirming the distinct genus status in a supplementary note in 1874.
facts.quote: He published these findings in a supplementary note, also in 1874

facts.statement: Hulke published a full osteology of the species in 1882.
facts.quote: Finally, in 1882 he published a full osteology of the species

facts.statement: While traditionally considered an early ornithopod, recent research has questioned this classification.
facts.quote: It has traditionally been considered an early member of the group Ornithopoda, but recent research has put this into question

facts.statement: Most known specimens of Hypsilophodon were discovered between 1849 and 1921.
facts.quote: Most known Hypsilophodon specimens were discovered between 1849 and 1921

facts.statement: The known specimens represent approximately twenty individual animals.
facts.quote: These represent about twenty individual animals.

facts.statement: Specimen NHM R5829 is the skeleton of a large Hypsilophodon individual.
facts.quote: NHM R5829, the skeleton of a large animal

facts.statement: Specimens NHMUK PV R 5830 and NHMUK PV R 196/196a are skeletons of juvenile Hypsilophodon.
facts.quote: NHMUK PV R 5830 and NHMUK PV R 196/196a, both skeletons of juvenile animals

facts.statement: Specimen NHMUK PV R R2477 consists of a skull block and two separate vertebral columns.
facts.quote: NHMUK PV R R2477, a block with a skull together with two separate vertebral columns

facts.statement: A specimen was found in 1900 in the Black Hills of South Dakota by George Reber Wieland.
facts.quote: The specimen was found in 1900 in the Black Hills of South Dakota, United States, by George Reber Wieland

facts.statement: It is debated whether H. wielandi is a distinct species of Hypsilophodon or synonymous with Camptosaurus valdensis.
facts.quote: Spanish Palaeontologist José Ignacio Ruiz-Omeñaca proposed that H. wielandi was not a species of Hypsilophodon but instead related to or synonymous with "Camptosaurus" valdensis from England

facts.statement: Fossils from the Isle of Wight are considered the only authentic Hypsilophodon fossils known.
facts.quote: This leaves the finds on Isle of Wight, off the south coast of England, as the only known authentic Hypsilophodon fossils.

facts.statement: Hypsilophodon fossils are found in the late Barremian (about 126 million years ago) in a marl layer on the Isle of Wight.
facts.quote: The fossils have been found in the Hypsilophodon Bed, a one-metre thick marl layer surfacing in a 1200 metre long strip along the Cowleaze Chine parallel to the southwest coast of Wight, part of the upper Wessex Formation and dating to the late Barremian, about 126 million years old.

facts.statement: A maximum length of 2.3 meters is often stated for Hypsilophodon.
facts.quote: For Hypsilophodon often a maximum length of 2.3 m is stated.

facts.statement: In 2009, Galton revised the maximum known length of Hypsilophodon down to 1.8 meters.
facts.quote: However, in 2009, Galton concluded that this femur in fact belonged to Valdosaurus and downsized Hypsilophodon to a maximum known length of 1.8 m

facts.statement: Typical specimens of Hypsilophodon are about 1.5 meters long.
facts.quote: Typical specimens are about 1.5 m long.

facts.statement: Gregory S. Paul estimated a weight of 20 kg for a 2-meter-long Hypsilophodon.
facts.quote: In 2010, Gregory S. Paul estimated a weight of 20 kg for an animal 2 m in length.

facts.statement: Hypsilophodon was a bipedal dinosaur that ran on two legs.
facts.quote: Like most small dinosaurs, Hypsilophodon was bipedal: it ran on two legs.

facts.statement: Hypsilophodon possessed a lightweight skeleton, low aerodynamic posture, long legs, and a stiff tail to aid running.
facts.quote: Numerous anatomical features aided this, such as: light-weight, minimized skeleton, low, aerodynamic posture, long legs, and stiff tail

facts.statement: The fifth finger of Hypsilophodon was opposable and could be used to grasp food items.
facts.quote: With Hypsilophodon the fifth finger had gained a specialised function: being opposable it could serve to grasp food items.

facts.statement: There is debate regarding whether the front teeth of Hypsilophodon had a specialized function.
facts.quote: although there is some debate as to whether these teeth may have had a specialized function in Hypsilophodon

facts.statement: The upper jaw of Hypsilophodon carried up to eleven teeth, while the lower jaw had up to sixteen.
facts.quote: The upper jaw carried up to eleven teeth in the maxilla; the lower jaw had up to sixteen teeth.

facts.statement: The rear teeth of Hypsilophodon were fan-shaped.
facts.quote: The teeth to the back were fan-shaped.

facts.statement: Hypsilophodon had a very large eye socket overshadowed by a palpebral bone equal to half its diameter.
facts.quote: The eye socket was very large. A palpebral with a length equal to half the diameter of the eye socket overshadowed its top section.

facts.statement: The vertebral column of Hypsilophodon included nine cervical, fifteen to sixteen dorsal, five to six sacral, and about forty-eight tail vertebrae.
facts.quote: The vertebral column consisted of nine cervical vertebrae, fifteen or sixteen dorsal vertebrae, six or five sacral vertebrae and about forty-eight vertebrae of the tail.

facts.statement: Long ossified tendons stiffened much of the back and tail of Hypsilophodon.
facts.quote: Much of the back and the tail was stiffened by long ossified tendons connecting the spines on top of the vertebrae.

facts.statement: The arrangement of tendons in the tail created a herring-bone pattern that completely immobilized the tail end.
facts.quote: resulting in a herring-bone pattern completely immobilising the tail end.

facts.statement: A long-held misconception was that Hypsilophodon was armoured.
facts.quote: A long-lived misconception concerning the anatomy of Hypsilophodon has been that it was armoured.

facts.statement: The internal plates found in Hypsilophodon are similar to those in Talenkauen and Thescelosaurus and were likely cartilaginous in origin.
facts.quote: Such plates are better known from Talenkauen and Thescelosaurus, and were probably cartilaginous in origin.

facts.statement: In modern classification, Hypsilophodon is considered a basal ornithopod.
facts.quote: Hypsilophodon in the modern view thus simply is a basal ornithopod.

facts.statement: In 2014, Norman proposed a monophyletic group called Hypsilophodontia to replace the historically complicated name Hypsilophodontidae.
facts.quote: In 2014, Norman resolved a monophyletic Hypsilophodontia (avoiding the name "Hypsilophodontidae" due to its complicated history).

facts.statement: A 2017 study by Madzia, Boyd, and Mazuch placed Hypsilophodon outside Ornithopoda as the sister taxon to Cerapoda.
facts.quote: In 2017, Daniel Madzia, Clint Boyd, and Martin Mazuch reassessed Hypsilophodon outside of Ornithopoda altogether, placing it in a more basal position, as the sister taxon to the Cerapoda

facts.statement: In 2023, Longrich and colleagues described Vectidromeus as a new ornithopod genus closely related to Hypsilophodon.
facts.quote: In 2023, Longrich et al. described Vectidromeus as a new coeval genus of ornithopod closely related to Hypsilophodon.

facts.statement: The species Hypsilophodon foxii was named by Thomas Henry Huxley in 1869.
facts.quote: species_authority: Huxley, 1869.

facts.statement: Hypsilophodon was a small bipedal dinosaur with a herbivorous or possibly omnivorous diet.
facts.quote: Era un pequeño animal bípedo con una dieta herbívora o posiblemente omnívora.

facts.statement: Hypsilophodon could reach lengths of up to 1.8 meters, weighed about 20 kilograms, and was an agile runner.
facts.quote: Hypsilophodon alcanzó hasta 1,8 metros de largo, pesaba unos 20 kilogramos y era un corredor ágil.

facts.statement: Hypsilophodon had a pointed head equipped with a sharp beak used for biting plant material, similar to modern parrots.
facts.quote: Tenía una cabeza puntiaguda equipada con un pico afilado que se usaba para morder material vegetal, como los loros modernos.

facts.statement: Early studies incorrectly suggested that Hypsilophodon could climb trees, had armor, reached lengths of 2.3 meters, and existed outside of the Isle of Wight.
facts.quote: Los estudios más antiguos han dado lugar a una serie de ideas erróneas sobre el Hypsilophodon, que era capaz trepar a los árboles, que estaba blindado, que alcanzaba una longitud de 2,3 metros y su presencia fuera de Wight.

facts.statement: Due to its small size, Hypsilophodon likely fed on low-growing vegetation, preferring high-quality plant material like young shoots and roots.
facts.quote: Due to its small size, Hypsilophodon fed on low-growing vegetation, in view of the pointed snout most likely preferring high quality plant material, such as young shoots and roots, in the manner of modern deer.

facts.statement: The Zahnreihen-spacing in Hypsilophodon was about 2.3, indicating a relatively low distance between teeth of the same eruption stage.
facts.quote: The Zahnreihen-spacing, the average distance in tooth position between teeth of the same eruption stage, was rather low with Hypsilophodon, about 2,3.

facts.statement: In 1971, Galton refuted earlier arguments, showing that the first toe was incorrectly reconstructed and that features like claw curvature were not adaptations for climbing, concluding Hypsilophodon was a bipedal running form.
facts.quote: In 1971 Galton in detail refuted Abel's arguments, showing that the first toe had been incorrectly reconstructed and that neither the curvature of the claws, nor the level of mobility of the shoulder girdle or the tail could be seen as adaptations for climbing, concluding that Hypsilophodon was a bipedal running form.

facts.statement: Due to their size and behavior, Hypsilophodon has often been referred to as the "deer of the Mesozoic".
facts.quote: For these reasons, the hypsilophodonts, particularly Hypsilophodon, have often been referred to as the "deer of the Mesozoic".

facts.statement: There was a debate over the opposability of the first toe in Hypsilophodon, with Heilmann denying it in 1926 and Abel refusing to accept this conclusion in 1927.
facts.quote: In 1926 Heilmann had again changed his mind, denying that the first toe was opposable because the first metatarsal was firmly connected to the second, but in 1927 Abel refused to accept this.

facts.statement: Hypsilophodon was often cited as reaching a maximum length of 2.3 meters.
facts.quote: Para el Hypsilophodon a menudo se indica una longitud máxima de 2,3 metros.

facts.statement: In 2009, Galton concluded that a previously attributed femur belonged to Valdosaurus, reducing the known maximum length of Hypsilophodon to 1.8 meters.
facts.quote: en 2009, Galton concluyó que, de hecho, este fémur pertenecía a Valdosaurus y reducía el tamaño de Hypsilophodon a una longitud máxima conocida de 1,8 metros

facts.statement: Typical specimens of Hypsilophodon measure around 1.5 meters in length.
facts.quote: Los especímenes típicos miden alrededor de 1,5 metros de largo.

facts.statement: Hypsilophodon would have reached a height of up to half a meter.
facts.quote: Hypsilophodon habría alcanzado hasta medio metro de altura.

facts.statement: In 2010, Gregory S. Paul estimated a weight of 20 kilograms for a Hypsilophodon two meters long.
facts.quote: En 2010, Gregory S. Paul estimó un peso de 20 kilogramos para un animal de dos metros de longitud.

facts.statement: Like most small dinosaurs, Hypsilophodon was bipedal and ran on two legs.
facts.quote: Como la mayoría de los dinosaurios pequeños, Hypsilophodon era bípedo, corría en dos piernas.

facts.statement: Hypsilophodon had a lightweight, low skeleton with an aerodynamic posture, long legs, and a rigid tail immobilized by ossified tendons to maintain balance.
facts.quote: Un esqueleto liviano, bajo, con postura aerodinámica, patas largas y cola rígida, inmovilizada por tendones osificados, para mantener el equilibrio.

facts.statement: In 1974, Galton concluded that Hypsilophodon was among the ornithischians best adapted for running.
facts.quote: En 1974, Galton concluyó que habría estado entre los ornitisquio mejor adaptados para correr.

facts.statement: Despite living in the last period when non-avian dinosaurs walked the earth, the Cretaceous, Hypsilophodon possessed a series of apparently "primitive" characteristics.
facts.quote: A pesar de vivir en el último de los periodos en que los dinosaurios no avianos caminaban por la tierra, el Cretácico, el Hypsilophodon tenía una serie de características aparentemente "primitivas".

facts.statement: For example, Hypsilophodon had five fingers on each hand and four toes on each foot.
facts.quote: Por ejemplo, había cinco dedos en cada mano y cuatro en cada pie.

facts.statement: In Hypsilophodon, the fifth finger had acquired a specialized function, being opposable and able to serve for grasping food.
facts.quote: En Hypsilophodon, el quinto dedo había adquirido una función especializada, ser oponible y podía servir para agarrar alimentos.

facts.statement: Additionally, despite having a beak like most ornithischians, Hypsilophodon still had five sharp triangular teeth at the front of the upper jaw, the premaxilla.
facts.quote: Además, a pesar de que tenía un pico como la mayoría de los ornitisquios, Hypsilophodon todavía tenía cinco dientes triangulares puntiagudos en el frente de la mandíbula superior, el premaxilar.

facts.statement: Further back, the upper jaw carried up to eleven teeth in the maxilla, while the lower jaw had up to sixteen teeth.
facts.quote: Más hacia la parte posterior, la mandíbula superior llevaba hasta once dientes en el maxilar superior. La mandíbula inferior tenía hasta 16 dientes.

facts.statement: The back teeth were fan-shaped.
facts.quote: Los dientes de la espalda tenían forma de abanico.

facts.statement: The skull of Hypsilophodon was short and relatively large.
facts.quote: El cráneo de Hypsilophodon era corto y relativamente grande.

facts.statement: The snout was triangular and pointed, ending in an upper beak whose cutting edge was notably lower than the row of upper teeth.
facts.quote: El hocico era triangular y puntiagudo, terminando en un pico superior cuyo borde de corte era notablemente más bajo que la fila de dientes superiores.

facts.statement: A brow ridge with a length equal to half the diameter of the eye socket shaded its upper section.
facts.quote: Un palpebral con una longitud igual a la mitad del diámetro de la cuenca del ojo ensombreció su sección superior.

facts.statement: An scleral ring of fifteen small bony plates supported the outer surface of the eye.
facts.quote: Un anillo esclerótico de quince pequeñas placas óseas apoyaba la superficie externa del ojo.

facts.statement: The vertebral column consisted of 9 cervical vertebrae, 15 or 16 dorsal vertebrae, 6 to 5 sacral vertebrae, and approximately 48 caudal vertebrae.
facts.quote: La columna vertebral consistía en 9 vértebras cervicales, 15 o 16 vértebras dorsales, 6 a 5 vértebras sacras y aproximadamente 48 vértebras caudales.

facts.statement: Much of the back and tail were rigid due to long ossified tendons connecting the spines on the top of the vertebrae.
facts.quote: Gran parte de la espalda y la cola estaban rígidas por largos tendones osificados que conectaban las espinas en la parte superior de las vértebras.

facts.statement: There were several rows of these in opposite directions, resulting in a fish-scale pattern that completely immobilized the tail tip.
facts.quote: Hubo varias filas contradireccionales de estas, lo que resultó en un patrón de espina de pescado que completamente inmovilizó el extremo de la cola.

facts.statement: A long-standing misconception about the anatomy of Hypsilophodon was that it was armored.
facts.quote: Un concepto erróneo de larga data sobre la anatomía de Hypsilophodon ha sido que estaba blindado.

facts.statement: As Galton pointed out in 2008, the supposed armor appears to be from the torso, an example of internal intercostal plates associated with the rib cage.
facts.quote: Como señaló Galton en 2008, la supuesta armadura parece ser del torso, un ejemplo de placas intercostales internas asociadas con la caja torácica.

facts.statement: Huxley originally assigned Hypsilophodon to the Iguanodontidae.
facts.quote: Huxley originalmente asignó Hypsilophodon a los Iguanodontidae.

facts.statement: In 1882, Louis Dollo erected a separate Hypsilophodontidae to include it.
facts.quote: En 1882, Louis Dollo erigío un Hypsilophodontidae separado para incluirlo.

facts.statement: In modern vision, Hypsilophodon is simply a basal ornithopod.
facts.quote: Hypsilophodon en la visión moderna, por lo tanto, simplemente es un ornitópodo basal.

facts.statement: In 2017, Daniel Madzia, Clint Boyd, and Martin Mazuch removed Hypsilophodon from Ornithopoda entirely, placing it as the sister group to Cerapoda in a more basal position.
facts.quote: En 2017, Daniel Madzia, Clint Boyd y Martin Mazuch eliminaron Hypsilophodon de Ornithopoda en conjunto, ubicándolo como el grupo hermano de Cerapoda , en una posición más basal

facts.statement: Hypsilophodon lived in the Cretaceous, the last period when non-avian dinosaurs walked the earth.
facts.quote: A pesar de vivir en el último de los periodos en que los dinosaurios no avianos caminaban por la tierra, el Cretácico

facts.statement: There is some debate over whether these front teeth had a specialized function in Hypsilophodon.
facts.quote: aunque existe cierto debate sobre si estos dientes pueden haber tenido una función especializada en el Hypsilophodon.

facts.statement: Its entire body was built for running, featuring a lightweight, low skeleton with an aerodynamic posture, long legs, and a rigid tail immobilized by ossified tendons to maintain balance.
facts.quote: Todo su cuerpo fue construido para correr. Un esqueleto liviano, bajo, con postura aerodinámica, patas largas y cola rígida, inmovilizada por tendones osificados, para mantener el equilibrio.

facts.statement: Hypsilophodon was a small herbivore that likely ate low vegetation, preferring high-quality plant material like young shoots and roots similar to modern deer.
facts.quote: Debido a su pequeño tamaño, el Hypsilophodon se alimenta de vegetación de baja, dado que el hocico puntiagudo probablemente prefiere material vegetal de alta calidad, como brotes jóvenes y raíces, a la manera de los ciervos modernos.

facts.statement: The skull structure of Hypsilophodon suggests it had cheeks, an advanced feature that would have helped it chew food.
facts.quote: La estructura de su cráneo, con los dientes colocados muy atrás en la mandíbula, sugiere fuertemente que tenía mejillas, una característica avanzada que habría facilitado la masticación de alimentos.

facts.statement: Like most dinosaurs and all ornithischians, Hypsilophodon continuously replaced its teeth in an alternating pattern moving from the back to the front of the jaw.
facts.quote: Como en casi todos los dinosaurios y ciertamente en todos los ornistisquios , los dientes fueron reemplazados continuamente en un arreglo alternativo, con las dos ondas de reemplazo moviéndose desde la parte posterior hacia la parte frontal de la mandíbula.

facts.statement: The average spacing between teeth in the same eruption stage was quite low in Hypsilophodon, approximately 2.3.
facts.quote: El espaciado de Z, la distancia promedio en la posición del diente entre los dientes en la misma etapa de erupción, fue bastante bajo con Hyspilophodon , aproximadamente 2,3.

facts.statement: This dentition would have allowed Hypsilophodon to process relatively hard plants.
facts.quote: Dicha dentición habría permitido procesar plantas relativamente duras.

facts.statement: In 1882, Hulke suggested Hypsilophodon was quadrupedal but could climb rocks and trees for shelter due to its hand structure.
facts.quote: En 1882, Hulke sugirió que el Hypsilophodon era cuadrúpedo pero, en vista de su mano, podía trepar rocas y árboles para buscar refugio.

facts.statement: In 1912, Austrian paleontologist Othenio Abel argued that Hypsilophodon was a fully arboreal animal because its first toe could function as an opposable hallux, suggesting an arboreal lifestyle was primitive for all dinosaurs.
facts.quote: En 1912 esta línea de pensamiento fue perseguida por el paleontólogo austríaco Othenio Abel. Concluyendo que el primer dedo del pie del pie podía funcionar como un hallux oponible, Abel declaró que el Hypsilophodon era un animal totalmente arbóreo e incluso que un estilo de vida arbóreo era primitivo para los dinosaurios en su conjunto.

facts.statement: In 1926, Heilmann changed his opinion, denying the first toe was opposable because the first metatarsal was firmly connected to the second, but Abel refused to accept this in 1927.
facts.quote: En 1926, Heilmann volvió a cambiar de opinión, negando que el primer dedo fuera opuesto porque el primer metatarsiano estaba conectado firmemente al segundo, pero en 1927 Abel se negó a aceptar esto.

facts.statement: In 1936, Swinton supported the idea that even a forward-pointing first metatarsal could carry a movable toe.
facts.quote: En 1936, fue apoyado por Swinton, quien afirmó que incluso un primer metatarsiano apuntando hacia adelante podría llevar un dedo movible.

facts.statement: In 1969, Peter M. Galton conducted a more precise analysis of the musculoskeletal structure, showing the body posture was horizontal.
facts.quote: Sin embargo, Peter M. Galton en 1969 realizó un análisis más preciso de la estructura musculoesquelética, mostrando que la postura del cuerpo era horizontal.

facts.statement: In 1971, Galton refuted Abel's arguments by showing the first toe was incorrectly reconstructed and that claw curvature, shoulder mobility, or tail could not be adaptations for climbing, concluding Hypsilophodon moved bipedally.
facts.quote: En 1971, Galton refutó detalladamente los argumentos de Abel, demostrando que el primer dedo del pie se había reconstruido incorrectamente y que ni la curvatura de las garras, ni el nivel de movilidad del hombro o la cola podían verse como adaptaciones para escalar, concluyendo que Hypsilophodon tenía una forma bípeda de moverse.

facts.statement: The level of parental care in Hypsilophodon is undefined as no nests have been found, though ordered nests of related species suggest some care was taken before hatching.
facts.quote: El nivel de cuidado parental en este dinosaurio no se ha definido, no se han encontrado nidos, aunque se conocen nidos ordenados de especies relacionadas, lo que sugiere que se tomó cierto cuidado antes de la eclosión.

facts.statement: Although Hypsilophodon fossils did not form part of a single herd, bones accumulated gradually, often leading to the belief the animals moved in large groups.
facts.quote: Aunque los fósiles de Hypsilophodon no formaban parte de una sola manada, los huesos se habían ido acumulando gradualmente, a menudo se consideraba probable que los animales se movieran en grandes grupos.

facts.statement: For these reasons, hypsilophodontids, particularly Hypsilophodon, are often referred to as the "Mesozoic deer".
facts.quote: Por estas razones, los hipsilofodóntidos, particularmente Hypsilophodon, a menudo se han referido como el "ciervo del Mesozoico".

facts.statement: Some indications of reproductive habits come from the possibility of sexual dimorphism, with Galton considering specimens with five instead of six sacral vertebrae, including one with a rib not touching the pelvis, likely representing females.
facts.quote: Algunas indicaciones sobre los hábitos reproductivos son proporcionadas por la posibilidad de dimorfismo sexual, Galton consideró probable que los ejemplares con cinco en lugar de seis vértebras sacras, con algunos especímenes, la vértebra que normalmente debería contar como la primera parte del sacro con una costilla que no toca la pelvis, representan a hembras.

facts.statement: The genus Hypsilophodon was named by Huxley in 1870.
facts.quote: PBDB name: Hypsilophodon (genus), Huxley 1870

facts.statement: The parent group of Hypsilophodon is Hypsilophodontidae.
facts.quote: Parent group: Hypsilophodontidae

facts.statement: Hypsilophodon belongs to the family Hypsilophodontidae.
facts.quote: Family: Hypsilophodontidae

facts.statement: Hypsilophodon is classified in the class Ornithischia.
facts.quote: Class: Ornithischia

facts.statement: Hypsilophodon lived from the Kimmeridgian to the Aptian, between 154.8 and 119.57 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Kimmeridgian to Aptian (154.8 to 119.57 million years ago)

facts.statement: There are 10 recorded fossil occurrences of Hypsilophodon.
facts.quote: Fossil occurrences recorded: 10

rejected.statement: Hypsilophodon was a small, agile bipedal herbivore measuring 1.5 to 2 meters long and weighing 20 kilograms.
rejected.quote: It was a small, agile bipedal herbivore, measuring 1.5 - 2 m long and weighing 20 kg
rejected.reason: statement copies the source wording: 'was a small agile bipedal herbivore measuring 1.5'

rejected.statement: Huxley first announced the new species in 1869, and the published text of that lecture serves as the official naming article.
rejected.quote: Huxley first announced the new species in 1869 in a lecture; the text of this, published the same year, forms the official naming article
rejected.reason: statement copies the source wording: 'Huxley first announced the new species in 1869'

rejected.statement: Hulke published a description of his new specimens in 1873.
